import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    orders = inputs["orders"].copy()
    price_list = inputs["price_list"].copy()
    
    # src: source data already in orders
    
    # exp: expression - normalize sku
    orders["sku_norm"] = orders["sku"].apply(
        lambda x: x.upper().strip() if pd.notna(x) else np.nan
    )
    
    # lkp: lookup with effective-dated tie-breaking
    orders["unit_price"] = np.nan
    orders["price_flag"] = "OK"
    
    for idx, row in orders.iterrows():
        sku_norm = row["sku_norm"]
        order_date = row["order_date"]
        
        # NULL sku_norm never matches
        if pd.isna(sku_norm):
            orders.at[idx, "unit_price"] = 0
            orders.at[idx, "price_flag"] = "NO_PRICE"
            continue
        
        # Find matching price_list rows
        # Normalize price_list sku for comparison
        price_list["sku_norm_lookup"] = price_list["sku"].apply(
            lambda x: x.upper().strip() if pd.notna(x) else np.nan
        )
        
        matches = price_list[
            (price_list["sku_norm_lookup"] == sku_norm) &
            (price_list["valid_from"] <= order_date)
        ]
        
        if len(matches) == 0:
            orders.at[idx, "unit_price"] = 0
            orders.at[idx, "price_flag"] = "NO_PRICE"
        else:
            # Tie-break: GREATEST valid_from, then LOWEST list_id
            matches = matches.sort_values(
                by=["valid_from", "list_id"],
                ascending=[False, True]
            )
            best_match = matches.iloc[0]
            orders.at[idx, "unit_price"] = best_match["unit_price"]
            orders.at[idx, "price_flag"] = "OK"
    
    orders.drop(columns=["sku_norm_lookup"], errors="ignore", inplace=True)
    
    # ext: expression - calculate extended amount
    orders["ext_amount"] = orders["qty"] * orders["unit_price"]
    # qty * unit_price where either is NULL gives NULL
    orders.loc[orders["qty"].isna() | orders["unit_price"].isna(), "ext_amount"] = np.nan
    
    # rtr: router - route based on conditions (evaluated IN ORDER)
    orders["route"] = "STANDARD"
    
    # Rule 1: price_flag == 'NO_PRICE' or qty is NULL or qty >= 100
    rule1 = (orders["price_flag"] == "NO_PRICE") | (orders["qty"].isna()) | (orders["qty"] >= 100)
    orders.loc[rule1, "route"] = "REVIEW"
    
    # Rule 2: ext_amount >= 1000 (only if rule1 not matched)
    rule2_mask = ~rule1 & (orders["ext_amount"] >= 1000)
    orders.loc[rule2_mask, "route"] = "BULK"
    
    # Rule 3: ext_amount < 50 (only if rule1 and rule2 not matched)
    rule3_mask = ~rule1 & ~rule2_mask & (orders["ext_amount"] < 50)
    orders.loc[rule3_mask, "route"] = "SMALL"
    
    # out1: order_enriched
    order_enriched = orders[["order_id", "sku_norm", "unit_price", "route"]].copy()
    
    # out2: aggregation on route and order_date
    agg_data = orders.groupby(["route", "order_date"], as_index=False).agg({
        "order_id": "count",
        "ext_amount": "sum"
    })
    agg_data.rename(columns={"order_id": "order_count"}, inplace=True)
    agg_data.rename(columns={"ext_amount": "total_ext"}, inplace=True)
    
    # SUM ignores NULLs; if all values are NULL, sum is 0
    agg_data["total_ext"] = agg_data["total_ext"].fillna(0)
    
    route_daily = agg_data[["route", "order_date", "order_count", "total_ext"]].copy()
    
    return {
        "order_enriched": order_enriched,
        "route_daily": route_daily
    }
